newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs seek better EU response to refugee crises.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs seek better EU response to refugee crises.

text.p: As the international community struggles to respond to a new refugee crisis on the Zaire-Rwanda border, the European Parliament called on November 12 for swift and effective European Union reaction to such emergencies.
MEPs approved an EU plan to help refugees in Asia and Latin America -- COM(95)297 -- but insisted the EU must on no account collaborate with attempts to make refugees return home by force.

"Governments are increasingly more worried about not having refugees and asylum seekers on their doorstep than about respecting the principle of not forcing people to return when they are in fear of their lives," British Socialist Richard Howitt, who reported on the plan to parliament, told Reuters recently.
On the advice of Howitt, who reported on the draft regulation for parliament, MEPs called for a string of amendments to the scheme.

As well as insisting the EU's first legislation on refugees should explicitly outlaw forced repatriation, MEPs demanded a simplification of the cumbersome bureaucratic structure for approving refugee aid projects worth over two million Ecus.

Refugee crises demand urgent action but under the projected approval procedure sought by ministers, the European Commission would have to get permission in the 11 official EU languages before it could release the aid, according to Howitt.
This would lead to a three-month delay in one in four projects and create 70,000 extra pieces of paperwork every year, he told the parliament on Monday evening.

In other amendments parliament said the EU should give priority to projects specifically designed to help women and children, who make up 80 percent of the population in refugee camps, and social groups which have been singled out for persecution.

Commissioner Christos Papoutis said on Monday the Commission was prepared to accept many of the amendments including those designed to outlaw forced repatriations and guarantee freedom from discrimination.
